h1: Future of Play-Based Learning in India's Schools: Challenges and Opportunities

props.title: Future of Play-Based Learning in India's Schools: Challenges and Opportunities
props.summaryText: NEP 2020 opened the door to play-based learning. The real obstacles schools face, from space and training to parents' expectations, and the opportunities ahead.
props.author: meera-iyer
props.imageAlt: Installer preparing ground for a new school playground

takeaways.text: Policy now supports play-based learning, especially for ages 3 to 8.
The main challenges are teacher training, space, large classes and parents' expectations of rote results.
Opportunities include better-designed outdoor spaces, low-cost materials and community support.
Small, consistent changes in timetable and space make a real difference.

faq.q: What are the challenges of play-based learning in India?
faq.a: Limited teacher training, small or unsuitable spaces, large class sizes, pressure from parents for rote results, assessment systems built around exams, and limited budgets for materials and play areas.

faq.q: What opportunities does NEP 2020 create for play-based learning?
faq.a: It legitimises play- and activity-based learning in the foundational stage, encourages new teaching materials and teacher training, and pushes schools to rethink classrooms and outdoor spaces.

faq.q: How can parents support play-based learning?
faq.a: By understanding that play builds real skills, asking teachers how play is used for learning, encouraging outdoor play at home, and valuing understanding over memorisation.
